title: Affine fibre chart with its prime and point dimension
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $x\in X$ and $s=f(x)$. Let $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ be affine open neighbourhoods [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $f(W)\subset V$. Assume that the induced $R$-algebra $A$ is finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ represent $x$ and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ represent $s$, so $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ for the induced ring map $\varphi$. Set $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, using the canonical identification $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $F=k\otimes_R A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The canonical morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is an open immersion onto the inverse image of $W$. It identifies the point of $X_s$ above $x$ with the prime $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$, where $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto\bar\lambda\bar a$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is induced by $\varphi$. This prime contracts to $\mathfrak q$ under $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. The algebra $F$ is finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}F)=\dim_x(X_s)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is a finite nonnegative integer. More precisely, any finite presentation $A=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$ induces $F\cong k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_m)$.

proof.text: Use Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso to identify the affine prime residue field, and compose it with the inverse of the equality transport and the residue-field isomorphism of the open immersion iV. Residue-field point naturality gives Spec(R → κ(p)) followed by iV equal to Spec(e.hom) followed by the canonical point map of s. The induced map κ(p) → κ(q) is R-linear by Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap and the scalar tower.

source.place: Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points), affine description before the lemma and the residue-field diagram after it.

proof.text: Apply pullbackSpecIso R κ(p) A with the residue field already as the first tensor factor. Map this affine pullback to Spec κ(s) ×_S X using Spec(e.hom), iW, and iV. The open-fibre-product lemma makes this an open immersion; its range is the intersection of the inverse images of the two ranges. Spec(e.hom) is an isomorphism and hence surjective, so its range contributes the whole space. Compose with pullback symmetry to obtain j into X_s. The two projection equations and the claimed range follow from the pullback map identities and the affine pullback isomorphism.

Construct ψ by Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap from the R-algebra map κ(p) → κ(q) and the canonical R-algebra map A → κ(q). Its pure-tensor formula is the defining formula of productMap. Its kernel is a prime ideal because κ(q) is a field. Evaluation on 1 ⊗ a is the canonical image of a in κ(q), which vanishes exactly when a belongs to q. Thus the kernel prime Q contracts to q.

source.place: Section Local rings, residue fields of primes and induced maps, together with Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product).

proof.text: By the first projection identity of j and the contraction calculation, the image of Q under the fibre projection is iW(q)=x. The fibre projection is an embedding by def-pc-scheme-fibre and also sends f.asFiber x to x. Its injectivity gives j(Q)=f.asFiber x directly, without introducing an auxiliary field-valued point.

For any given finite presentation P, use P.baseChange κ(p), which is already a presentation of κ(p) ⊗_R A in the required tensor order. Its relations span its evaluation kernel. Transport the quotient along that equality of ideals and use its quotientEquiv, restricted to κ(p), to get E. The base-changed generator formula proves E(X a)=1 ⊗ P.val a. Finite presentation implies finite type, and finite type is stable under tensor base change.

source.place: Tag 05G3 (section-base-change), presentation formula immediately after Definition 05G4 (definition-base-change).

proof.text: The open immersion identifies $\operatorname{Spec}F$ homeomorphically with $O$. Each open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak Q$ corresponds to an open neighbourhood of $j(\mathfrak Q)$ in $O$, with the same Krull dimension by homeomorphism invariance. Taking the minima in the definition of dimension at a point gives $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}\operatorname{Spec}F=\dim_{j(\mathfrak Q)}O$. The open-subspace dimension lemma gives $\dim_{j(\mathfrak Q)}O=\dim_{j(\mathfrak Q)}X_s=\dim_x(X_s)$, where step 4 identifies the point.

source.place: Tag 0055 (definition-Krull), part (4) and the open-neighbourhood observation following it.

proof.text: Apply the finite-type affine point-dimension theorem to the field $k$, the finite type $k$-algebra $F$ from step 5, and its prime $\mathfrak Q$ from step 3. It states that this topological dimension at the point is a nonnegative integer (the maximum of the dimensions of the components containing it). Together with step 6 this proves finiteness and nonnegativity on both sides. The existence of $\mathfrak Q$ ensures that the chart and all neighbourhoods at issue are nonempty.
